note: N-016 / R12. `bump` declares a local named like each property before reading it: `const target = n + 1n; assert(target == this.target)` and `const count = n; this.count = this.count + count; assert(this.count > count)`. Before N-016 every tier resolved `this.target` / `this.count` to the same-named LOCAL's stack slot, so the target guard compiled to OP_DUP OP_NUMEQUAL (always true: any n spent) and the continuation committed n + n instead of old + n. The accepts pin the committed state by hand from the source (old count + n); the business near-miss is the exact input the pre-fix script accepted; the tampered-output reject proves the continuation is committed to by hashOutputs.
